title: credit depreciation and velocity notes
content:
Quick scratchpad: trying to bake a way to think about credits that (a) feel simple for users, (b) map back to tokens+SLO economics for us, and (c) handle 'stale'/unused credits without being punitive. Notes to self, not for org yet.

Goals and constraints:
- credits should be easy to explain in marketing (chunks, monthly allotment, rollover rules)
- internal mapping must allow converting to expected token demand so we can forecast GPU capacity and revenue leakage
- prefer a decay model for leftover credits over hard expirations (reduce churn friction)
- handle multi-model routing (small fast model vs large expensive model) — credits should reflect expected per-route cost

Key assumptions (placeholder numbers, will refine):
- avg host model cost to Redwood (amortized infra + HW + ops) = $0.0025 per 1k tokens for small model, $0.012 per 1k for large model (includes KV/caching amortization).
- price we want to maintain for starter-like offering: $0.006 per 1k tokens (blended).
- 1 credit ~ equivalent to 100 tokens (nicer numbers for UX). So 1k tokens = 10 credits.

Implication: internal cost per credit:
- small model: $0.0025 / 10 = $0.00025 per credit
- large model: $0.012 / 10 = $0.0012 per credit
- blended target margin at price $0.006 per 1k ($0.0006 per credit) -> gross margin depends on model mix.

Example tier sketches (rough):
- Starter: 1,000 credits / mo (covers ~100k tokens) priced $6/mo (maps to $0.06 per 10k tokens? — this is intentionally simple).
- Growth: 10k credits / mo priced $50/mo (bulk discount, expect heavier use of cached batching).
- Teams: 100k credits / mo priced $400/mo (commit, SLA on p50 latency).

Rough unit economic check (Starter):
- User uses 60% small model, 40% large model (by token volume)
- blended cost per credit = 0.6*$0.00025 + 0.4*$0.0012 = $0.00061 per credit
- cost for 1k credits = $0.61 -> if we charge $6 for 1k credits, gross margin ~ 90% (seems high; sign we undercharged model cost? check numbers).

Session / conversation framing: credits consumed per session should reflect both tokens and SLO. Two levers: token burn + session keepalive surcharge (to account for KV cache memory and routing overhead). Proposal:
- token burn: 1 credit per 100 tokens (same as above)
- session surcharge: 0.2 credits per active minute (to reflect connection/slot * ops overhead)
Example: 2-min chat with 600 tokens out and 400 tokens in -> token burn = 10 credits, time surcharge = 0.4 credits -> total ~10.4 credits.

Credit depreciation / shelf-life idea (primary novel bit):
- credits roll over for 90 days but decay linearly by 1%/day after month 1 (so months 2-3 gradually lose value). Rationale: encourages usage without hard cutoff; reduces long-term liability.
- accounting rule: count expected decay when booking deferred revenue; assume 40% of rolled credits will be used within 30 days, 25% in 31-60, 10% in 61-90, remainder decays (model for liability).

Velocity model (for capacity planning):
- target: translate committed credits into GPU-hours needed. Need conversion: tokens per GPU-hour.
- measured: on p3/4-like fleet for small model, we get ~45M tokens per GPU-hour (batchy interactive mix). For large model ~8M tokens/GPU-hour.
- therefore credits per GPU-hour (small model): 45M tokens / 100 tokens-per-credit = 450k credits per GPU-hour. For large model: 80k credits per GPU-hour.
- example: 1k-credit starter pool used fully => 0.0022 GPU-hours for small-model dominated traffic (tiny). But when aggregated across 10k starters could be non-trivial.

Pricing levers and experiments to run:
1) Convert credits -> time-decayed credits UX: show 'freshness' meter in console (green -> yellow -> red) to drive usage. Measure churn delta if we allow decayed rollover vs hard expiration.
2) Per-route pricing: allow customers to pin credits to model families (e.g., 80% credits for small, 20% for large) and charge a premium for auto-upgrades (allows predictable capacity mapping).
3) Session bundling: offer session packs (50 sessions) for low-latency interactive apps — each session includes a fixed time-surcharge budget and token budget; simpler for UX.

Open questions / risks:
- Complexity: UX may confuse customers if credits decay; must show simple equivalence to tokens and a simulator.
- Abuse: credits-as-money could be exploited by automated loops; need per-route rate limits and fraud detection.
- Model-mix skew: customers might game the system by routing to cheap models when heavy usage, then spike to expensive ones; need overage pricing or dynamic reweighting.

Immediate todo (next week):
- run sanity script: map 50 existing starter customers -> historical token mix -> estimate realized cost vs revenue under proposed credit equivalence (owner: Samir).
- instrument console mockup for freshness meter (owner: Maya).
- draft customer-facing FAQ language explaining decay and rollover (owner: me).

Notes to self: keep numbers intentionally round for UX (100 tokens = 1 credit). Avoid tiny decimals on pricing pages. Make sure to include an explicit conversion table in billing UI.

Random brainstorm lines:
- promotion idea: "double-freshness" on sign-up month (credits don't decay first 60 days) to boost trial usage.
- enterprise commit: allow credits to be bucketed and fully non-decaying if they take an annual discount + SLA (makes accounting simpler for enterprise).

End of scratchpad. Will iterate with real telemetry and mark up the model-mix numbers with per-route historical data next pass.

Questions for PM: what is acceptable margin floor for starter tiers? set a target gross margin %, then solve for per-credit price.
summary: scratchpad exploring a credit unit tied to 100 tokens, decay/rollover rules, session surcharge, conversion to GPU-hours, and experiments to validate pricing UX and unit economics.
